bandReport.notes:
Band covers items 1-25 across rendered pages 1-5, which are booklet pages (3-A), (5-A), (7-A), (9-A) and (11-A) - i.e. the English pages only, consecutive with no gap. Items per page: p1 = 1-5, p2 = 6-10, p3 = 11-16, p4 = 17-20, p5 = 21-25.

BOUNDARIES. Item 1 opens at the top of p01-c1 and is whole. Item 25 ends on p05-c2 with all four of its options, the last being '(d) An order from the feudal lord to his subordinates'; nothing of it continues overleaf. I checked p06-c1 (a page I do NOT own) purely to confirm the boundary: page 6 opens at item 26 ('With reference to the book "Desher Katha"...'), so no item is stranded between this band and the next. I have not transcribed anything from page 6.

COLUMN CROPS. No crop was sliced; all text was read from the c1/c2 crops, with pNN.png used only for structure. Every crop shows the expected thin sliver of the neighbouring column down its far margin (line-end letters, and on p01-c1/p03-c1/p04-c1/p05-c1 the bare item numbers of c2). Two item numbers were themselves clipped by the split and were confirmed against the whole page: on p01-c2 the '4.' of item 4 is partly cut and the '5' of item 5 is cut away entirely, leaving only its full stop - both confirmed as items 4 and 5 against p01.png. The gutter sat at x=824-826 on all five pages, so the detection was stable across my band.

PRINTED DEFECTS / ODDITIES, all transcribed verbatim and not corrected: item 9's lead-in reads 'to which of the following type of citizens ?' (singular 'type'); item 19 statement 2 names the statute as 'the Representation of People Act, 1951', omitting 'the' before 'People'. Item 18's statements 1 and 2 are flat contradictions of each other - that is the question's design, not a misprint. Item 16 options (a) and (d) are close but genuinely distinct ('has no legal effect' vs 'has no legal effect independently of other parts'). No duplicated option and no item with a missing fourth option anywhere in this band; all 25 items carry exactly four options.

HOUSE STYLE. This booklet sets a space before ':' and '?' ('Consider the following statements :', 'correct ?'); preserved as printed. Curly quotes in the booklet are transcribed as plain ASCII quotes, matching the dominant convention of the sibling bands in this corpus. Item 24 sets its regnal numbers with a spaced en dash ('Mahendravarman - I') and its option sequences likewise; preserved.

TABLES. Item 10 prints a genuine two-column grid under italic headings 'International agreement / set-up' and 'Subject', joined by an em dash; rendered as a GFM pipe table with those headings, the em dashes dropped because the pipes carry that role. Item 21 prints the same grid shape but with NO column headings, so it is rendered with an EMPTY header row rather than invented headings - the separator row is mandatory for the renderer and inventing 'Term'/'Description' would add text the paper does not print. This follows the precedent already set elsewhere in this corpus.

SUBTOPICS. Two items use a label not in catalog.json and are flagged individually: item 3 (MPLADS) and item 10 (a mixed bag of international agreements spanning health, chemical weapons, climate and child rights). Both subjects and chapters are copied exactly from the catalog.
